key_insight: Low-dimensional capping makes 3D perovskite surfaces rougher while enhancing photoluminescence and preserving electronic uniformity, even under accelerated aging.
engineering_relevance: Surface smoothness alone may be an unreliable quality metric for designing durable, electronically uniform perovskite solar absorbers.
method: Form mixed-dimensional heterostructures using 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium-derived Ruddlesden–Popper capping layers.
Combine statistical AFM with spatially resolved confocal photoluminescence spectroscopy.
Compare pristine and capped films before and after accelerated aging.
evidence_signal: Despite increased roughness and height asymmetry, capped films showed enhanced PL, reduced non-radiative recombination, and more uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting, with better retention of optoelectronic homogeneity during aging.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify device-efficiency gains or establish whether accelerated-aging behavior translates to operational solar-cell lifetimes.
paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
